# Pilot amendment 3: explicitly accepted local target

Declared after the identified Codex upstream-readiness rejection and before the
next trial. Accepted Decapod source already supports a review-bound
`proof.repository_contract.canonical_local_target` policy. The earlier seed did
not select it. This is a fixture configuration gap, not evidence that native
local proof is unavailable or that any source-CI obligation should be waived.

Create a fresh private seed from the original committed task. Review and accept
local-target authority on its canonical master before agent invocation, recompute
the command-contract review digest through native reconciliation, and preserve
every required Rust test/toolchain/source obligation. This setting applies only
to this explicitly local disposable consumer fixture; Decapod source remains on
its unchanged required Buildkite profile. Do not retrofit policy on the prior
agent branch or erase its refused attempt.

Use a stable explicit host actor, the same natural cold objective and independent
checker. Capture executable digests before launching this new trial. Retain its
separate protocol identity and policy transition; it is not pooled into the
unidentified-actor pair. A native failed test is an engineering rejection only
when the test actually executes. Full readiness, a passing fixed checker and
observable context/custody remain separate acceptance observations. No model or
kernel statement alone is independent proof.
